faq.q: Is the redaction truly irreversible, or just a layer on top?
faq.a: It's permanent. On export the visible canvas — with your blur, pixelation or fill baked in — is re-encoded into a brand new image file, so the original pixels under a redacted area no longer exist and there's no hidden layer to recover. This is unlike a black box over PDF text, which leaves the real text selectable underneath.

faq.q: What redaction modes and selection shapes are there?
faq.a: Modes: blur (adjustable 2–40px radius, applied in three passes), pixelate (4–50px block), black out, white out, solid colour fill, and an emoji sticker cover. Shapes: rectangle and ellipse (click-drag), freehand brush (adjustable size, hold and paint), and polygon/lasso (click points, double-click to close). There's also undo/redo (up to 20 steps) and zoom.

faq.q: Does it remove GPS and EXIF data?
faq.a: Yes. With 'Remove all metadata' ticked (on by default), the output is regenerated from a clean canvas, which drops EXIF, GPS location and camera info along with it — no separate step needed. Output can be PNG, JPEG or WEBP, with a quality slider for the lossy formats and a size estimate.

faq.q: What does Auto-detect do, and can I trust it?
faq.a: It's a rough heuristic, not OCR — it scans for horizontal bands with high edge density (typical of text lines) and proposes candidate boxes you can accept individually or all at once. The tool states plainly it may miss sensitive data or flag harmless areas, so you must check the result yourself. For batch work, your redactions are recorded as relative coordinates and re-applied to every loaded image at the same fractional position, downloadable as a ZIP.
